summary: Shift from static boat preferences to reactive 7-day trailing performance tracking; book hottest class based on recent YT/angler, not date guessing.
describe: Season 1 showed 3/4-day dominated (1055 YT) and overnight was surprisingly good per-trip (4.7 YT/trip). But date selection matters: days 64 and 71 were skunks despite booking the best class. Strategy: at each tick, calculate recent 7-day YT per angler for each trip class. Book tomorrow's offer for the hottest class if trailing average is positive. Prefer San Diego/Malihini for 3/4-day, any scheduled boat otherwise. Use half-days only if premium classes dead. Commit PTO on weekdays when signals warrant.
